setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. Counsel wants the jury to believe the mechanic’s account of what happened. The mechanic is not a party, and none of the hearsay exceptions applies.

transcript.speaker: Q
transcript.text: When you spoke afterward, what did the mechanic tell you about the bicycle brakes?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: They told me, “A brake cable separated at its clamp.”

explanation: The absent nonparty’s assertion is offered for its truth without an exception. (FRE 802)
trap_note: Hearing a statement firsthand does not make its factual assertion firsthand evidence.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. Both sides accept that the note is genuine. Counsel wants its unsigned account accepted as true, but no hearsay exception applies.

transcript.speaker: Q
transcript.text: What did the unsigned note say about the bicycle brakes?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: It said, “A brake cable separated at its clamp.”

explanation: An authenticated note can still contain inadmissible hearsay. (FRE 802)
trap_note: Authentication resolves origin, not the hearsay issue.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. The witness is repeating a colleague’s account of what a neighbor said. Neither speaker is a party, and neither statement falls within a hearsay exception.

transcript.speaker: Q
transcript.text: What did your colleague tell you they had heard about the bicycle brakes?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: They said their neighbor told them, “A brake cable separated at its clamp.”

explanation: Each hearsay layer needs an applicable exclusion or exception. (FRE 805)
trap_note: An exception for only one layer would not cure the other.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. The person who shouted saw the incident firsthand and was still frightened and overwhelmed when they spoke.

transcript.speaker: Q
transcript.text: What did you hear the person beside the bicycle brakes shout?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: They were shaking and crying. They shouted, “A brake cable separated at its clamp.”

explanation: A statement about a startling event made under its stress qualifies as an excited utterance. (FRE 803(2))
trap_note: The declarant need not be unavailable.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. The person speaking was watching the incident and described it as it happened.

transcript.speaker: Q
transcript.text: What did the person watching the bicycle brakes say as it happened?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: They said, “A brake cable separated at its clamp.” They were describing it right then.

explanation: A contemporaneous description of a personally perceived event may be a present sense impression. (FRE 803(1))
trap_note: Excitement is unnecessary for this exception.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. The plaintiff is introducing the defendant’s own statement against the defendant.

transcript.speaker: Q
transcript.text: What did the defendant tell you about the bicycle brakes?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: “I failed to tighten the brake cable.”

explanation: An opposing party’s own statement offered against that party is excluded from hearsay. (FRE 801(d)(2)(A))
trap_note: It need not have been against the speaker’s interest when made.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. Counsel wants to use their own client’s earlier denial to prove the client was not responsible. No hearsay exception applies.

transcript.speaker: Q
transcript.text: What did my client tell you about the bicycle brakes?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: “I had nothing to do with what happened.”

explanation: A party cannot invoke the opposing-party exclusion to offer its own favorable statement. (FRE 801(d)(2)(A))
trap_note: The exclusion requires offering the statement against the party who made it.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. Counsel offers an absent employee’s report to prove what happened. Both sides agree the report is genuine; apart from the business-records argument, no hearsay exception applies.

transcript.speaker: Q
transcript.text: Why was this report about the bicycle brakes written?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: The lawyer asked for it after the lawsuit started. We do not normally make reports like this.

explanation: A narrative prepared solely for litigation does not become a business record merely by being filed. (FRE 803(6))
trap_note: Routine storage is not the same as routine creation.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. Counsel wants this earlier statement accepted as proof that the incident happened, rather than as evidence of how the speaker felt. No other hearsay exception applies.

transcript.speaker: Q
transcript.text: What did your colleague say the next day about the bicycle brakes?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: “I remember it clearly. A brake cable separated at its clamp.”

explanation: The state-of-mind exception generally does not admit a remembered fact to prove that fact. (FRE 803(3))
trap_note: Present memory differs from present intention.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. The jury needs to know why the witness started an inspection. The warning is offered only to explain that decision, not to prove the warning was true.

transcript.speaker: Q
transcript.text: What made you go and look at the bicycle brakes?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Someone called to warn me about it. That is why I went over to check.

explanation: A warning offered only to explain relevant responsive conduct is not offered for its truth. (FRE 801(c)(2))
trap_note: The jury must not use the warning to prove the alleged danger.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. The hobby does not help explain what happened, what the witness could see, or whether the witness has a reason to lie.

transcript.text: After your work with the bicycle brakes, what hobby did you spend the evening on?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: I was making a wire mobile.

explanation: An unrelated personal activity does not make a consequential fact more or less probable. (FRE 401–402)

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. The cousin had no involvement in the events. Their childhood collection has no connection to any disputed issue.

transcript.text: You have told us about the bicycle brakes, what did your cousin collect as a child?

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. The parties disagree about how the incident happened. This witness was there and watched it happen.

transcript.text: What did you see happen to the bicycle brakes?

transcript.speaker: A

explanation: A firsthand observation bearing on the disputed mechanism has a tendency to prove a consequential fact. (FRE 401)
trap_note: Relevant evidence need not settle the whole case.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. The school lunchbox has no connection to the incident, the witness’s memory, or any other issue in the case.

transcript.speaker: A

explanation: The unrelated lunchbox design has no bearing on this dispute. (FRE 402)
trap_note: A memorable detail is not necessarily a relevant one.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. The childhood toy has no connection to the dispute and does not help test the witness’s honesty or memory.

transcript.speaker: Q

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: I called it Ivory Cricket.

explanation: The unrelated toy’s name does not help establish any disputed consequential fact. (FRE 401–402)
trap_note: Personal knowledge alone does not establish relevance.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. Counsel wants the jury to conclude that the defendant acted carelessly this time because the defendant is generally careless. Character itself is not an issue, and no character-evidence exception applies.

transcript.text: People who know them say they are careless.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. Counsel offers an unrelated earlier incident only to suggest that the defendant is the sort of person who damages property.

transcript.speaker: Q
transcript.text: Before this dispute about the bicycle brakes, did the defendant damage something else?

transcript.text: A painted toy train, in a separate incident years ago.

explanation: A prior act cannot be used solely to show propensity to commit this act. (FRE 404(b)(1))

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. Counsel wants the jury to decide this dispute based on the plaintiff’s supposedly greedy personality. Character itself is not an issue, and no exception permits this use.

transcript.text: In this dispute about the bicycle brakes, what do people generally say about the plaintiff’s attitude to money?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: That the plaintiff is greedy.

explanation: General character cannot ordinarily prove disputed conduct through propensity. (FRE 404(a)(1))

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. The other side has already introduced testimony attacking a witness’s reputation for honesty. The person now testifying knows that witness’s community well.

transcript.text: You know the witness who testified about the bicycle brakes. What is their reputation for telling the truth?

transcript.text: People in our community consider them honest.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. Counsel wants to prove an earlier lie using a separate document. The document is genuine, but the lie has no relevance beyond honesty and did not result in a criminal conviction.

transcript.text: Does this document prove that the witness who described the bicycle brakes lied on another occasion?

transcript.text: What is Arlo Quinn’s reputation for honesty in your community?

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. Counsel wants to introduce a photograph, but there is no other witness or evidence establishing what it shows.

transcript.text: Can you tell us whether this photograph shows the bicycle brakes?

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. The witness was at a dental appointment throughout the incident and has no firsthand knowledge of it. Counsel nevertheless asks them to describe what happened.

transcript.text: What happened to the bicycle brakes during the incident?

transcript.text: Someone deliberately damaged it before anyone else arrived.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. Counsel wants to connect a recorded voice to a particular person. No other evidence identifies the speaker; assume there is no separate hearsay problem.

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. The photograph shows a condition that matters to the case. This witness personally saw that condition at the time.

transcript.text: Does this photograph accurately show the bicycle brakes as you saw it?

transcript.speaker: A

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. The witness could neither see nor hear inside the enclosure and has no firsthand knowledge of what happened there. Counsel asks for an account of the events, not an expert opinion.

transcript.text: What happened to the bicycle brakes inside the enclosure?

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. This person is testifying as an ordinary witness. Counsel has not qualified them as an engineering expert.

transcript.speaker: A

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. The witness personally saw the person’s behavior, and whether that person was intoxicated matters to the case. No medical diagnosis is requested.

transcript.text: How did the person handling the bicycle brakes seem to you?

setting: Federal bicycle injury trial. A brake cable separated at its clamp. The witness has no clinical training and has not been qualified as an expert. Counsel asks them to diagnose a psychiatric condition.
